fyNote: Financial year ends 30 June. FY2025 = July 2024 to June 2025. FY2024 restated.
segmentNote: A utilities group: Singapore power and UK water earn most of the money; data centres and AI are the new growth areas (AR p.10-11, p.18).

how.title: How YTL Power makes money
how.text: Revenue = electricity sold in Singapore + water and sewerage bills in the UK and Johor + mobile and broadband subscriptions + data centre services

items.label: Cost of sales
items.tip: Fuel and gas for power plants, electricity bought, running the water network, staff and depreciation of plants and pipes.

items.label: Finance costs
items.tip: Interest on about RM38bn of borrowings, including UK bonds linked to inflation.

items.label: Other operating costs
items.tip: Including allowances for unpaid bills and foreign exchange losses.

items.label: Tax
items.tip: Tax in Singapore, the UK and Malaysia.

items.label: Partners' share of profit
items.tip: Profit belonging to minority shareholders, for example in Ranhill.

items.label: Profit to shareholders
items.tip: What is left for shareholders: paid as dividends or kept to grow the business.

pnl.incomeNote: Plus about RM4.38 per RM100 of revenue from other income and associates.

fiveYear.note: Dividend per share (sen): 2021 4.5 · 2022 4.5 · 2023 6.0 · 2024 7.0 · 2025 8.0. FY2024 was boosted by unusually high Singapore electricity prices.

rows.name: Power generation
rows.tip: YTL PowerSeraya power plants and the Geneco electricity retailer in Singapore, plus power in Johor.

rows.name: Water and sewerage
rows.tip: Wessex Water in south-west England and Ranhill's water business in Johor; back in profit in 2025.

rows.name: Investment holding
rows.tip: Investments, data centres and other activities.

rows.name: Telecommunications (Yes)
rows.tip: Mobile and broadband in Malaysia; still loss-making.

segments.note: Profit here is profit before tax by segment. About 85% of revenue is earned outside Malaysia (AR p.18).

assets.label: Power plants, pipes and other property
Money owed by customers and others

balance.note: Utilities borrow heavily against steady, regulated income: borrowings of RM38bn are larger than shareholders' funds. Wessex Water's regulated asset base (GBP4.7bn) supports much of this debt (AR p.10).

waterfall.l: Power plants, data centres and networks

cash.wfNote: Operations produced RM4.2bn of cash, but spending on power plants, data centres and networks rose to RM6.7bn, funded with RM6.1bn of new borrowing.

metrics.label: Market value
metrics.plain: What the whole company costs at today's share price: RM37.3 billion.

metrics.label: P/E (FY2025 profit)
metrics.plain: You pay about RM15 for every RM1 of yearly profit. A high number means investors expect growth.

metrics.label: EPS (FY2025)
metrics.plain: Profit earned for each share you own over the year.

metrics.label: Dividend yield (FY2025 dividends)
metrics.plain: For every RM100 of shares, about RM1.8 a year comes back as cash dividends.

metrics.label: Payout ratio FY2025
metrics.plain: Of every RM100 profit, about RM27 is paid out; the rest is kept to grow.

metrics.label: Price to book
metrics.plain: The share price is 1.7 times the accounting value of what shareholders own.

metrics.label: Return on equity FY2025
metrics.plain: For every RM100 shareholders have in the company, it earned about RM12 profit last year.

metrics.label: Net margin FY2025
metrics.plain: What is left as profit for shareholders from every RM100 of revenue: RM11.68.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Revenue compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Profit growth FY2025
metrics.plain: Profit to shareholders compared with the year before.

metrics.label: Net debt
metrics.plain: Borrowings minus cash: RM25.74 billion owed to lenders after using all its cash.

metrics.label: Net gearing
metrics.plain: Net debt is 119% of shareholders' funds. Under 50% is usually seen as comfortable; above 100% means lenders fund more than owners.

metrics.label: Free cash flow FY2025
metrics.plain: Cash from operations minus spending on assets and land: RM-2,471 million. Negative means it borrowed or used savings to fund growth.

metrics.label: Free cash flow yield
metrics.plain: That spare cash as a share of the company's market value.

metrics.label: EV / EBITDA
metrics.plain: A price tag that includes debt: about 9.3 times its yearly cash earnings before interest and tax.

drivers.evidence: Power generation profit fell from RM3.69bn to RM2.76bn after last year's exceptionally high prices (AR p.10, p.18)
drivers.why: The biggest earner; prices are normalising.

drivers.evidence: Water and sewerage swung from a RM101m loss to RM384m profit as UK inflation on index-linked bonds eased (AR p.10, p.18)
drivers.why: A regulated, steady business returning to profit.

drivers.evidence: Wessex Water asked for its 2025-2030 plan to be referred to the Competition and Markets Authority (AR p.10)
drivers.why: The outcome sets how much it can spend and charge for five years.

drivers.evidence: Wessex Water's regulated asset base grew about 9% to GBP4.7bn (AR p.10)
drivers.why: Allowed returns grow with the asset base.

drivers.evidence: Full-year consolidation of Ranhill; rising industrial demand in Johor (AR p.10-11)
drivers.why: Malaysia's share of revenue rose from 4% to 15%.

drivers.evidence: YTL Green Data Center Park in Kulai and YTL AI Cloud with NVIDIA GB200 systems (AR p.11)
drivers.why: A new growth engine riding AI demand, but needs heavy investment.

drivers.evidence: Spending on plants and property rose to RM6.7bn from RM3.5bn (AR p.167)
drivers.why: Builds future income but used more cash than operations produced.

drivers.evidence: Borrowings RM38.0bn vs shareholders' funds RM21.6bn (AR p.162)
drivers.why: Normal for utilities, but higher interest rates would hurt.

drivers.evidence: Telecommunications lost RM256m (RM326m in FY2024) (AR p.18)
600MW hydrogen-ready plant in Singapore targeted for end-2027 (AR p.11)
drivers.why: Replaces older capacity and supports long-term earnings.

drivers.evidence: About 85% of revenue is from overseas (AR p.18)
drivers.why: Changes in the Singapore dollar and pound affect ringgit profit.

drivers.evidence: About 15 times FY2025 profit at RM4.35 (see Valuation)
drivers.why: Investors weigh steady utilities against data-centre growth hopes.

competitors.name: Other Singapore power generators and retailers (e.g. Tuas Power, Senoko, Keppel)
competitors.source: General market knowledge, not the report

competitors.name: Data-centre developers in Johor
competitors.how: Compete for hyperscale and AI customers

outlook.text: Renewable energy momentum expected to continue in Singapore and Malaysia; 600MW hydrogen-ready plant due by end-2027 (AR p.11).
YTL Green Data Center Park and the AI cloud business are progressing well (AR p.11).
Wessex Water awaits the competition regulator's decision on its 2025-2030 plan (AR p.10).
The global outlook remains uncertain, with higher trade restrictions (AR p.38).

outlookOverall.text: Management describes performance as sound and points to growth in renewables, Johor water and data centres (AR p.10-11).
